t: A policy is repudiated within three years under Section 45 for a misstatement that does not amount to fraud. The insurer must
o: forfeit all premiums
refund the premiums collected, within 90 days of repudiation
pay 50% of the sum assured
pay the surrender value only
e: Where repudiation is on grounds of mis-statement or suppression not amounting to fraud, premiums paid must be refunded within 90 days.

t: With effect from 22 September 2025, the GST applicable on premiums of individual life insurance policies (including term plans) is
o: nil (exempt)
e: The GST Council exempted individual life and health insurance premiums from GST effective 22 September 2025; this is a recent change.

t: The maximum benefit payable under the Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI) scheme is currently
o: ₹2.5 lakh
₹7 lakh
₹3.6 lakh
₹10 lakh
e: EDLI pays a minimum of ₹2.5 lakh and a maximum of ₹7 lakh to the nominee of a deceased PF member.

t: The premium paid for a critical illness rider attached to a life policy is deductible under
o: Section 80C
Section 80CCC
Section 10(10D)
Section 80D
e: Health-related rider premiums qualify under 80D (medical insurance), not 80C.

t: A proposer does not mention that another insurer declined his proposal six months earlier. This is
o: immaterial, since each insurer underwrites independently
non-disclosure of a material fact, breaching utmost good faith
a breach of insurable interest
permissible as the proposal form did not require it
e: A previous decline or postponement is a material fact that would influence a prudent underwriter.

t: Two persons claim to be assignees of the same policy. Under Section 38, priority between them is decided by
o: the date of the assignment deed
the amount of consideration paid
the date on which notice of assignment was received by the insurer
the age of the assignee
e: An assignment is effective against the insurer only on receipt of written notice, and priority follows the order of notices.

t: The HbA1c test called for in medical underwriting indicates
o: kidney function
liver enzyme levels
average blood glucose control over the previous two to three months
cholesterol level
e: Glycated haemoglobin reflects long-term sugar control and is used to assess diabetes risk.

t: Where death is due to an accident or other unnatural cause, the documents required include
o: FIR, post-mortem report and the police final/inquest report
the agent's confidential report
a succession certificate
the policyholder's PAN card
e: Unnatural deaths require police and medical-legal records to establish the cause and circumstances.

t: A life assured who has paid total premiums of ₹1,20,000 dies by suicide 8 months after the policy commenced. The amount payable is at least
o: Nil
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). 80% of ₹1,20,000 = ₹96,000 is the minimum payable under the suicide clause.

t: The Insurance (Amendment) Act 2021 raised the permissible foreign direct investment in an Indian insurance company to
e: FDI was 26% originally, raised to 49% in 2015 and to 74% by the 2021 amendment; 100% was proposed in Budget 2025.

t: A 'combi product' approved by IRDAI is
o: a ULIP combined with a mutual fund
a term plan with a housing loan
two life policies from the same insurer
a combination of a life insurance product and a health insurance product of two different insurers sold under one proposal
e: Combi products bundle a life insurer's product with a general/health insurer's product; each insurer remains liable for its own portion.

t: When underwriting a proposal on the life of a minor child, the insurer checks that
o: the child has an independent income
the child has passed a medical examination
the proposer parent has adequate insurance on his or her own life
the child has signed the proposal form
e: Insurance on a child without the parent being adequately insured raises moral hazard and reverses the normal protection logic.

t: A proposer born on 1 July 1985 takes a policy commencing on 1 February 2026. His age last birthday is
o: 39 years
41 years
40 years
42 years
e: He completed 40 years on 1 July 2025; age last birthday is 40, whereas age nearer birthday would be 41 since seven months have passed.

t: Under the 'open market option' permitted by IRDAI for pension plans, at vesting the policyholder may
o: withdraw the entire corpus in cash
transfer the corpus to a mutual fund
purchase the annuity from another insurer with up to 50% of the corpus
defer vesting indefinitely
e: IRDAI allows up to 50% of the vesting corpus to be used to buy an immediate annuity from any other insurer.

t: In a children's deferred assurance plan, the 'vesting date' is the date on which
o: the policy ownership passes to the child on attaining majority
the risk on the child's life commences
the first survival benefit is paid
the proposer's premium waiver starts
e: Vesting transfers ownership to the child (usually at age 18); risk commencement is a separate, often earlier, date.

t: The main drawback of the natural premium system is that
o: the insurer cannot build any reserve in early years
the premium is the same at all ages
the premium rises each year and becomes unaffordable at older ages
it cannot be used for term assurance
e: Under natural premium each year's premium equals that year's mortality cost, so it keeps increasing with age.

t: Under the IRDAI Protection of Policyholders' Interests Regulations 2024, a death claim not requiring investigation must be settled within
o: 15 days of receipt of all documents
30 days of receipt of all documents
60 days of intimation
90 days of intimation
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The 2024 regulations tightened the earlier 30-day norm to 15 days, and to 45 days where investigation is required.

t: A policyholder nominated his son, then aged 12, and appointed his brother as appointee. The policyholder dies when the son is 20. The claim is paid to
o: the appointee brother
the son directly, as he is now a major
the legal heirs
the court, under Section 47
e: The appointee's role is only to receive money during the nominee's minority; once the nominee attains majority, the appointee has no role.

t: Under IRDAI's 2019 linked product regulations, the minimum death benefit for a regular premium ULIP (entry age below 45 or otherwise) is
o: 10 times the annualised premium
7 times the annualised premium
5 times the annualised premium
1.25 times the annualised premium
e: The 2019 regulations fixed the minimum sum assured at 7 × annualised premium for regular premium policies and 1.25 × for single premium.

t: An extra premium charged for a hazardous occupation is normally expressed as
o: a flat amount per ₹1,000 sum assured
a percentage of the bonus
a percentage of the surrender value
a multiple of the policy loan
e: Occupational extras are flat per-mille charges on the sum assured, unlike age-related health extras which may be a percentage of the premium.

t: Experience rating in group insurance means that
o: premium is based on the age of the youngest member
all groups pay the same premium rate
renewal premium is adjusted based on the claims experience of that particular group
premium is fixed for the life of the scheme
e: Large groups are priced on their own claims history, with profit sharing or loading at renewal.

t: Where there is no nomination and the claim amount is large, the insurer may insist on a succession certificate, which is issued by
o: the Tahsildar
IRDAI
a competent civil court (District Judge)
the municipal corporation
e: Succession certificates are granted by the civil court under the Indian Succession Act; for small amounts insurers may accept an indemnity bond instead.

t: 'Loan-cum-revival' is possible when
o: the policy has been lapsed for more than five years
the surrender value of the lapsed policy is sufficient to grant a loan that covers the arrears of premium with interest
the policy is a term assurance
the policyholder has no other policies
e: The insurer grants a policy loan and adjusts it against arrears; any balance arrears must be paid by the policyholder.

t: Under the IRDAI Protection of Policyholders' Interests Regulations 2024, life insurers are required to
o: issue all policies in electronic form, with a physical copy on request
issue only physical policy bonds
issue electronic policies only for ULIPs
issue electronic policies only above ₹10 lakh sum assured
e: Mandatory electronic issuance applies to all policies from 1 April 2024; policyholders may still ask for a physical document.

t: For a one-year term assurance of ₹5,00,000 at a mortality rate of 4 per 1,000, the net single premium ignoring interest and expenses is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). ₹5,00,000 × 4/1,000 = ₹2,000.

t: An 'accelerated' critical illness rider differs from an 'additional' critical illness rider in that
o: the accelerated benefit is paid in addition to the base sum assured
the accelerated benefit has no survival period
the accelerated rider has no premium
the accelerated benefit is paid out of, and reduces, the base sum assured
e: Accelerated CI advances part of the death benefit; additional CI pays an extra amount without touching the base cover.

t: Among ULIP fund options, the one carrying the highest investment risk is the
o: liquid / money market fund
equity (growth) fund
debt (bond) fund
balanced fund
e: Equity funds invest predominantly in shares and are most volatile; liquid funds carry the least risk.

t: A ULIP issued in 2022 with annual premium of ₹4 lakh pays a death claim in 2026. The death benefit is
o: taxable as capital gains
taxable as income from other sources
exempt only up to ₹2.5 lakh
fully exempt, as the premium caps under Section 10(10D) do not apply to death benefits
e: The ₹2.5 lakh ULIP and ₹5 lakh non-ULIP premium caps apply to maturity/survival proceeds, not to sums received on death.

t: Other things being equal, who will receive the highest annual annuity per ₹1 lakh of purchase price under an immediate life annuity?
o: a 55-year-old annuitant without return of purchase price
a 70-year-old annuitant without return of purchase price
a 70-year-old annuitant with return of purchase price
a 55-year-old annuitant with return of purchase price
e: Higher entry age means shorter expected payment period, and dropping the return of purchase price removes a benefit, so the rate is highest.

t: The sum assured under a term rider attached to a base policy
o: must equal at least twice the base sum assured
has no limit
must equal the fund value
cannot exceed the sum assured of the base policy
e: Rider benefits are restricted so that the rider cannot become larger than the base contract.

t: The claim settlement ratio published for a life insurer is calculated as
o: claims paid divided by premium income
claims repudiated divided by claims received
claims paid divided by total policies in force
number of claims paid divided by number of claims received during the year
e: The claim settlement ratio compares the number of death claims paid with the total number of claims intimated in that financial year.

t: Under the PPHI Regulations 2024, an insurer must resolve a policyholder's grievance within
o: 3 days of receipt
14 days of receipt
30 days of receipt
90 days of receipt
e: The 2024 regulations shortened the grievance resolution timeline to 14 days; unresolved complaints may go to the Ombudsman.

t: A limited payment endowment has a 15-year policy term with premiums payable for 10 years. Sum assured is ₹6,00,000 and 4 annual premiums have been paid. The paid-up sum assured (excluding bonus) is
e: Paid-up SA = SA × premiums paid ÷ premiums payable = ₹6,00,000 × 4/10 = ₹2,40,000; the denominator is the premium-paying term, not the policy term.

t: The phenomenon that recently underwritten lives show lower mortality than lives of the same age insured many years ago is called
o: anti-selection
the selection effect
mortality drag
reversion
e: Medical selection at entry produces lighter mortality for some years; select tables capture this effect.

t: An increasing term assurance is primarily designed to
o: cover a reducing housing loan
provide maturity benefit
reduce premium at older ages
protect the real value of cover against inflation
e: The sum assured increases by a fixed percentage each year so the cover keeps pace with rising costs.

t: A policy of ₹1,00,000 earns compound reversionary bonus of 5% per annum for two years. The total vested bonus at the end of two years is
Under a policy effected under Section 6 of the Married Women's Property Act 1874, the beneficiaries can only be
o: the wife and/or children of the policyholder
the parents of the policyholder
any nominee named by the policyholder
the policyholder's creditors
e: An MWP policy creates a trust in favour of the wife and children, protecting the proceeds from creditors and other heirs.

t: Third-party insurance is compulsory for a motor vehicle used in a public place under which section of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988?
o: Section 140
Section 146
Section 163A
Section 166
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 146 makes TP cover compulsory; Section 164 fixes no-fault compensation (₹5 lakh death / ₹2.5 lakh grievous hurt).

t: An annual premium of ₹30,000 has been paid for 4 years. If the applicable GSV factor is 50%, the guaranteed surrender value of premiums (before bonus) is
Under a 'joint life last survivor' annuity, the annuity payments
o: continue until the death of both annuitants
stop on the first death
are paid for a fixed term only
are paid to the nominee after both deaths
e: Payments continue as long as either annuitant is alive; often the survivor receives 50% or 100% of the original annuity.

t: In which relationship is insurable interest presumed by law without proof of financial dependence?
o: husband and wife
brother and sister
uncle and nephew
landlord and tenant
e: Spouses are presumed to have unlimited insurable interest in each other's lives; other relatives must show pecuniary interest.

t: A reversionary bonus, once declared and vested, is
o: payable immediately in cash
payable along with the sum assured on death or maturity
revocable by the insurer in later years
payable only if future premiums are paid
e: Vested reversionary bonus is a guaranteed addition payable with the claim; it is not withdrawn once declared.

t: A policy loan is NOT available against
o: a regular premium term assurance policy
an endowment policy that has acquired surrender value
a whole life policy after three years
a money-back policy with vested bonus
e: Loans are granted against surrender value; term plans (and ULIPs) have no loan facility.

t: As of 2025, the number of life insurers registered with IRDAI (including LIC) is approximately
e: There are around 26 life insurers (LIC plus 25 private insurers) operating in India; 57 is the total of all insurers including general, health and reinsurers.

t: Since 1 April 2021, the standard fire policy for a dwelling in India is:
o: Standard Fire and Special Perils Policy
Bharat Griha Raksha
Bharat Sookshma Udyam Suraksha
Householder's Package Policy
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Bharat Griha Raksha for homes; Bharat Sookshma Udyam Suraksha (up to ₹5 crore) and Bharat Laghu Udyam Suraksha (₹5–50 crore) for enterprises.

t: Under a Salary Savings Scheme (SSS) arrangement for life insurance premiums
o: the insurer deducts premium directly from the employee's bank account
the employee pays yearly premium through the employer
the employer pays the entire premium as a perquisite
the employer deducts the monthly premium from salary and remits it to the insurer
e: SSS is a payroll deduction arrangement; monthly mode is permitted, usually without the normal monthly loading.

t: The 'discharge voucher' obtained before paying a claim is
o: the insurer's internal approval note
a receipt signed by the claimant acknowledging the amount in full and final settlement
the hospital's discharge summary
a court order permitting payment
e: The discharge voucher evidences settlement and protects the insurer from a second claim on the same policy.

t: A medical examination for a life insurance proposal should be conducted by
o: any registered doctor chosen by the proposer
a doctor on the insurer's panel, not the proposer's own family physician
the proposer's family physician
the agent, using a checklist
e: Panel doctors are independent of the proposer, which reduces the chance of a biased report.

t: A proposal 'accepted at ordinary rates' (OR) means
o: the policy is issued with a health extra
the proposal is accepted with a lien for five years
the life is standard and no extra premium, lien or exclusion is imposed
the policy is issued only on a term plan
e: OR acceptance is the normal outcome for a standard life after underwriting.

t: In a life insurance contract, insurable interest must exist
o: only at the time of the claim
both at inception and at the time of claim
at the time the contract is effected (inception)
at every premium due date
e: Unlike marine insurance, life insurance requires insurable interest only at inception; it need not exist when the claim arises.
